company.name: Ironleaf Manufacturing
company.summary: You run a metal parts manufacturing company in Ohio, USA. Your team does CNC machining and sheet metal work for customers who send drawings and RFQs, and you quote custom parts. About 160 employees handle production, quality, purchasing, sales engineering, planning and finance.
offerings: Custom metal parts quoted from customer drawings
company.customers: Industrial OEMs and equipment makers that need custom metal parts, mostly in Ohio and nearby states.
tech_signals: CNC controls such as Fanuc or Haas
Calipers, micrometers, and CMM for inspection

roles.title: Maintenance Technician
repetitive_tasks: Fix CNC and sheet metal equipment

strategy.executive_summary: Ironleaf Manufacturing runs custom metal parts work through Epicor, email RFQ intake, CAD drawings, and Excel quoting. Your team already has strong ERP and shop floor habits, but too much RFQ, scheduling, quality, purchasing, and finance work is still manual and scattered across inboxes and spreadsheets. The practical path is to add AI agents that read emails, extract drawing and PO details, draft updates, and log data into Epicor and Excel, with your people reviewing anything customer-facing or production-critical. Start with RFQ intake and daily scheduling because they touch the most revenue and capacity decisions. Keep the scope tight: assistants that prepare work, not systems that make final decisions.

maturity.label: Early
maturity.note: You have Epicor, Outlook, Excel, and CAD/CAM in daily use, but AI is not part of regular work. Most automation is manual entry or basic ERP transactions, with no agents reading email, drawings, or supplier messages.

opportunities.title: RFQ intake and quote prep
opportunities.description: An agent watches your RFQ inbox, opens attachments, extracts part numbers, quantities, material, and due dates, then creates a draft quote record in Epicor and a quote prep sheet in Excel. It also drafts an acknowledgement email that asks for missing drawing details.
before: Customer Service Rep checks shared RFQ inbox
Estimator reads drawing notes and calculates basic material
Estimator types quote notes into Excel
Estimator enters quote header in Epicor
after: Agent logs RFQ and extracts key fields from email and drawing
Agent creates draft quote sheet and Epicor quote header
Agent drafts acknowledgement with missing questions
Human: Sales Engineer reviews drawing and quote notes
Human: Estimator finishes cycle time and pricing

opportunities.title: Daily schedule and late job alerts
opportunities.description: An agent reviews open work orders and material availability in Epicor each morning, builds a short schedule summary, and flags jobs at risk of missing a date. It emails the summary to supervisors and updates a shared Excel schedule board.
before: Planner reviews open orders in Epicor
Scheduler sequences jobs on whiteboard or Excel
after: Agent pulls open orders, material, and due dates from Epicor
Agent creates morning schedule summary and risk list
Agent updates shared Excel schedule board
Human: Planner reviews risks and adjusts sequence
Human: Supervisor assigns jobs at shift start

opportunities.title: Production count and scrap entry
opportunities.description: An agent reads end-of-shift count sheets, texts, or emails from operators and enters production counts and scrap into Epicor or Excel. Supervisors get a clean daily summary instead of chasing paper.
after: Operator sends counts by text, email, or simple form
Agent parses counts and scrap by job
Agent enters data into Epicor or Excel
Agent sends daily summary to supervisor
Human: Supervisor reviews and corrects exceptions

opportunities.title: Invoice matching and AP exceptions
opportunities.description: An agent matches vendor invoices to purchase orders and receipts in Epicor, flags price or quantity mismatches, and drafts vendor questions. It prepares an exception list so AP can focus on real problems.
before: AP opens vendor invoice email or mail
AP matches invoice to PO and receipt in Epicor
AP writes vendor email for mismatches
AP enters invoice or holds it
after: Agent reads invoice and matches to Epicor PO and receipt
Agent flags mismatches with reason codes
Agent drafts vendor question email
Human: AP approves clean invoices and sends vendor questions
Human: Controller reviews exception summary

opportunities.title: Supplier PO follow-up and expediting
opportunities.description: An agent monitors late purchase orders in Epicor, drafts supplier follow-up emails with PO line details, and logs replies and new promise dates. It gives buyers a daily exception list instead of a full open PO report.
before: Buyer checks each supplier email thread
after: Agent pulls late POs from Epicor
Agent drafts supplier follow-up with line details
Agent logs supplier replies and promise dates
Agent creates daily shortage list
Human: Buyer reviews exceptions and escalates

opportunities.title: Quote follow-ups and order status answers
opportunities.description: An agent tracks open quotes and orders in Epicor, sends polite follow-up emails on a set cadence, and drafts status replies using current work order and shipment data. Your team approves anything that changes a promise date.
before: CSR writes follow-up emails one by one
CSR checks Epicor for order status
CSR asks planning for date changes
after: Agent pulls open quote and order list from Epicor
Agent drafts follow-up or status email with current data
Agent flags orders needing a human date decision
Human: CSR reviews and sends replies
Human: CSR updates customer on exceptions

opportunities.title: Nonconformance and corrective action logging
opportunities.description: An agent turns inspector notes, photos, and email into draft nonconformance records in Epicor or Excel, routes them to the right quality engineer, and tracks corrective action due dates. It sends reminders and updates the log when steps close.
before: Inspector writes NCR on paper or email
Quality Engineer types NCR into log
after: Agent reads inspector email or form and creates draft NCR
Agent routes NCR to assigned Quality Engineer
Agent sends reminders on open actions
Human: QE reviews, edits, and approves NCR
Human: QE closes record after verification

opportunities.title: Preventive maintenance reminders and repair logs
opportunities.description: An agent tracks preventive maintenance dates for CNC and sheet metal equipment, sends reminders to technicians, and turns repair emails into draft work logs. It keeps a simple downtime and parts list updated.
before: Technician writes repair note on paper
after: Agent sends PM reminders from equipment list
Agent creates draft repair log from email or text
Agent flags repeat downtime by machine
Human: Technician completes repair and confirms parts used
Human: Manager reviews downtime report

opportunities.title: Calibration due date tracking
opportunities.description: An agent tracks gauge and calibration due dates, sends reminders before expiry, and updates the calibration log when certificates arrive. It helps you avoid finding an overdue gauge during an audit.
before: Tech schedules outside calibration by email
after: Agent reads gauge list and calibration dates
Agent sends due and overdue reminders
Agent drafts outside calibration request
Agent updates log when certificate email arrives
Human: Calibration Tech confirms calibration and files record

roadmap.title: Fix the revenue and schedule front door
items: Connect agent to shared RFQ inbox and extract fields into Excel draft
Build quote prep template and Epicor quote header draft
Set up daily schedule summary from Epicor open work orders
Train Sales Engineering and Planning on review steps
Measure baseline quote response time and schedule update time

roadmap.title: Add quality, purchasing, and production data agents
items: Launch NCR logging and corrective action reminders
Launch late PO follow-up and supplier promise tracking
Launch production count and scrap entry from shift messages
Keep human approval on all customer and supplier messages
Review error rates weekly and adjust rules

roadmap.title: Extend to finance and maintenance
items: Launch invoice matching exception list with AP review
Launch PM reminders and repair log drafts
Create monthly savings and quality dashboard
Decide what to expand based on measured hours saved

risks.risk: Agents read the wrong field from a drawing or email and draft a bad quote.
risks.mitigation: Keep estimator approval before any quote goes out. Start with extraction only and compare against manual review for the first 4 weeks.

risks.risk: Epicor integration is harder than expected, causing delays.
risks.mitigation: Start with Outlook, Excel, and CSV imports. Add direct Epicor writes only after the workflow is proven.

risks.risk: Supervisors and operators do not trust automated counts or logs.
risks.mitigation: Use a simple review screen and daily exception report. Let supervisors correct entries before they affect planning.

risks.risk: Customer or supplier receives an automated message with wrong tone or data.
risks.mitigation: Use draft-only mode for all external emails. A named person sends every message until error rate is low.

risks.risk: Data quality in Epicor, BOMs, or calibration list limits agent accuracy.
risks.mitigation: Clean the top 20 used records first. Assign one owner per data set and review monthly.
